tone_statements.quote: - des positions coda traversées par des tons. Ce qui nous amène à ne pas limiter l’unité porteuse du ton à la voyelle ni à l’étendre à la syllabe, mais à la more, une unité intermédiaire entre les deux entités phonologiques évoquées.

sources.citation: Gawa, Djahéma. 2025. Issue of tone bearing units in Moba and Nawdm: a comparative analysis / Problème des unités porteuses de ton en moba et nawdm: une étude comparative. Ziglôbitha, Revue des Arts, Linguistique, Littérature & Civilisations (RA2LC) n°016, vol. 2 (décembre 2025): 05-18. Korhogo: Université Peleforo Gon Coulibaly.
sources.note: Argues, against Kantchoa (1994, 2005) who transcribed tones on obstruents (b̀ bāá 'they fell', bíg̀ 'child', púób̀ 'women'), that obstruents are not TBUs in Moba: an inaudible reduced vowel (schwa) carries the tone, so vowels are the main TBUs, with syllabic nasals and [l] also able to bear tone; data are marked with H (acute), M (macron) and L (grave) but the tone inventory itself is not discussed. Drawn from ch. 4 of the author's 2016 Lomé thesis.

tone.quote: Here, the sounds [d; r; m; f; s; l] get their sonority from vowels. So, vowels are the main TBUs in both Moba and Nawdm. However, the study reveals that some nasals and the liquid [l] can stand for syllable nuclei and therefore, be TBUs.

sources.note: Not opened (no online text). Clements & Rialland 2008 (author copy p. 33, sect. 3.3.2) cite this chapter as the source of their Moba example: Moba is 'a four-level Gur language' whose extra-H tone arose when the redundantly extra-high realisation of H before L (still visible in three-level Gulmancema, e.g. ò kándì vs Moba ù ka̋nt) was phonologised after loss of final vowels; final M became floating L. So the chapter is the diachronic account of Moba's fourth tone level (tonogenesis by loss of the Gulmancema-type final 'vocalic punctuation').
